INSIDE METAHRISE

A VR onboarding game built for MCMC — in photos, from the headset fitting to the leaderboard at the end.

Client
MCMC
Technology
Unity · Multiplayer VR
Year
2024
Read time
6 min

145 new hires, one onboarding day, and a brief that asked for something MCMC's induction had never been before: memorable.

The old version was a room, a deck, and a printed handbook — familiar territory for anyone who's sat through a corporate induction. It covered the material. It didn't make anyone remember it. MCMC came to EDT wanting new employees to leave day one actually knowing the company, not just having sat through a summary of it.

Built to be played, not watched

EDT built MetaHRise as a multiplayer VR onboarding game — new hires move through interactive scenarios modelled on real workplace situations, brand values, and department-specific roles, together, in the same session. The multiplayer structure wasn't incidental. Onboarding is also the first time a cohort meets each other, and a shared game does more for that than a shared slideshow ever could.

Every scenario in the build ties back to something measurable — a value, a workflow, a role responsibility — so the game isn't just entertaining, it's teaching, and MCMC could actually track whether it worked.

Onboarding is usually the least memorable day at a new job. MCMC wanted it to be the opposite — the day people actually talk about.

— EDT, on the MetaHRise brief
What it actually moved

The numbers held up outside the headset, which is the part that matters. Role comprehension in post-induction assessments went from 48% to 83%. Onboarding efficiency improved by 40% against the previous process. And 93% of the 145 employees who went through it rated the experience positively — high enough that MCMC has kept it as the standard induction, not a one-off pilot.

What came after

MetaHRise went on to win Management Initiative of the Year — Malaysia in 2025, and holds a Malaysia Book of Records entry from 2024. Neither was the brief. They're what happens when an onboarding problem gets treated as a design problem instead of a content problem.
